newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Prods Outlook - Gasoline stocks support prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Prods Outlook - Gasoline stocks support prices.

text.p: U.S. spot refined products trading started slowly Monday, with market players closely eyeing gasoline prices for signs of bullishness.
Product traders kept to the sidelines Monday as they sought firm bid and offer figures following the basis roll from February to March NYMEX contracts over the weekend.

Gasoline prices firmed nearly 0.50 cent by early afternoon Monday on the modest strength in the NYMEX, and traders said gasoline prices should strengthen as the summer driving season draws closer, helped by paltry inventory levels.
The latest American Petroleum Institute gasoline inventory figures sat at 201.297 million barrels, about 11 million barrels below the year-ago level.
"Gasoline is going to have a pop to the upside," said John Dosher, senior analyst with Pace Consultants in Houston.
Any refinery problems that occur in the next few weeks could speed the process, he said.
"Any little thing can cause it," Dosher said. "It's not a matter of if, it's a matter of when," he added.
March heating oil futures slipped about 0.75 cent a gallon by early afternoon to 65.41 cents a gallon amid mild weather in the key Northeast market.

But some traders were confident diffs might get a boost from a Weather Express Inc forecast of much-below-normal temperatures in the eastern half of the United States early next week upon arrival of an Arctic cold front.
Others cautioned that any widening in diffs would likely be short lived unless cold weather persisted.

"If that turns out to be just a little cold blip before it warms back up again, diffs are going to fall hard because we have enough (distillate) inventories and much more imported crude is coming in," said Nizam Sharief, an analyst and trader for Hornsby & Co.

In the Midwest Group Three market, inventories of low sulphur diesel fuel on hand in the region's key pipeline system have been steadily drawn down in recent weeks after hitting a seasonal high last month.

The Williams pipeline system opened the week with about 40 days' supply of low sulphur diesel fuel on hand after placing restrictions on shipments heading into the Group market from Gulf Coast refineries last month.
The draw in diesel stocks boosted basis last week and put some support under spot prices that have largely been tracking NYMEX heating oil futures, traders said.
"There should be some strength in diesel basis moving forward, and gasoline is firming, too, as refineries begin to cover for (maintenance) turnarounds," one Group Three trader said.
